page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose cloud compute instance designed for balanced multi-threaded compute and memory throughput. The server is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, offering 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance displays exceptional memory subsystem throughput, scoring 2993.05 on the PassMark memory test and delivering 195.06 GB/sec in large-block uncached write memory bandwidth, placing it in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Compression and decompression pipelines also demonstrate strong performance, with single-threaded gzip throughput reaching 40.52 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 283.74 GB/sec.

Compute benchmarking reveals solid multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 62,261.68 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 48,789.2. CPU-based AI inference performs well on compact architectures, processing 4,079.87 prompt tokens per second on small 135M models and sustaining 52.68 tokens per second generation on medium 7B models. In-memory data structures perform reliably, demonstrated by 62.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 80.02 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

A notable hardware tradeoff is the local storage footprint: the instance bundles only 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and excludes dedicated GPUs. Consequently, workloads requiring large persistent file systems or dense databases must rely on network-attached block storage. The instance provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for memory-intensive computations and distributed services that decouple compute from persistent disk storage.

The Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is well configured for high-concurrency web serving, in-memory caching tiers, parallel data compression tasks, continuous integration build clusters, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose virtual server built on AMD EPYC architecture, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores at 2.0 GHz and 128.0 GB of system RAM. Configured with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it includes AVX-512 vector acceleration, SHA-NI cryptography, and a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD boot disk without dedicated GPUs. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high write bandwidth reaching 195.06 GB/sec, alongside rapid single-threaded gzip compression of 40.52 GB/sec and 62.56 million Redis SET operations per second. While the 1 GB local storage capacity necessitates external storage for stateful workloads, the instance delivers high compute and memory density. It is suited for in-memory caching, web serving, compression pipelines, and CPU-driven inference tasks.
